answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding one active identity to each non-transferable lease of a surveyed plot. The registry hashes the lease ID and rejects a duplicate; every epoch the agent signs a challenge with the key the registry bound to that lease. An attacker's voyage across many plots still pays a separate per-epoch fee C, and a basalt marker on a terrace grants no extra slot because only the lease ID counts. With a fixed per-identity reward R, total reward is n(R-C), deterring only while R<C; a rich attacker can still lease many plots up to the registry's published cap.
